c1.title: A call from the previous city that lands after New City is still counted in the new city's ledger
c1.detail: Round-1 finding, not fixed and not in the fixed or rejected lists. setup() clears the ledger and keeps the same client connected. A mayor, resident or chat call that was in flight before New City still ends in GmiClient._log, which emits call_logged unconditionally, so the old city's call (latency, error, repairs, tokens, role) is added to the new city's counts and health. brain_calls._ask discards the stale answer by _generation but the ledger does not look at it. Effect is small and transient (at most the calls in flight at the reset) but the first numbers of a fresh city are not purely its own. Confirmed by reading the code path, not re-run.
c1.lens: LEDGER CORRECTNESS AND HOT PATH (round 2: fixes verified)

c1.title: Street Orders column reads '-' on every pre-ledger save until new turns land (disclosed regression of the fix)
c1.detail: To make league Orders and Arena accept% agree, league Orders now reads the ledger's orders_ok/orders_rejected, which start at zero on a save without brain.ledger, whereas the old column showed the sim's whole-city history. For a returning player, or a loaded autosave on the 12 Nov demo machine, the league shows '-' (and the Arena shows '-') for each mayor until it lands a live or replayed turn after loading. The unit lists this under remaining_risks; I confirmed it by reading decorate(): from_ledger is true whenever the flag is on, so there is no fallback to the sim's counters when the ledger has no orders yet. A fresh demo city is unaffected.
c1.lens: LEDGER CORRECTNESS AND HOT PATH (round 2: fixes verified)

c1.title: Cheaper but still above the old parse; WASM cost unmeasured; NaN is reported as 'trailing_comma'
c1.detail: After the fix GmiReply.read costs about 1.5x extract_json on every 200 reply (0.33 vs 0.22 ms at 1.8 KB, 1.7 vs 1.13 ms at 9.6 KB, native headless, spread <0.02 ms), mostly the cached-regex pre-filter and the info dict. That closes the 4-5x round-1 finding (+0.1 to +0.6 ms native per reply, was +5 to +13 ms). The WASM multiplier is still not measured, and the owner's complaint was web smoothness, so a quick web probe would settle it. Separately, a reply containing NaN/Infinity is labelled 'trailing_comma' (documented in the file header), so the Arena's repair kinds name a fix that was not a comma.
c1.lens: LEDGER CORRECTNESS AND HOT PATH (round 2: fixes verified)

c1.title: With model_ledger off, a ledger loaded from an older save still feeds Speed and the health light, contradicting the flag and runbook text
c1.file: scripts/ai/model_ledger.gd (from_dict has no enabled() check); scripts/fp/reporter/league_ledger.gd decorate (speed and health are not gated)
c1.detail: The model_ledger flag text and docs/runbooks/model-ledger.md say that when it is off, 'Speed reads -' and 'the lights read idle'. from_dict does not check the flag, and decorate takes speed_ms, speed and health from the ledger whatever from_ledger says (only Orders is gated). A save made with the flag on and loaded with GRIDFALL_FLAGS=model_ledger=off therefore shows the old numbers in the street league, and it keeps writing them back into the save (to_dict is ungated). The new fp_league_ledger_test flag-off check clears the ledger first, so it cannot see this.
c1.repro: Probe: scratchpad c1/review-tests-claims/r2/probe2.gd. Ledger with 6 live mayor answers at 9 s, to_dict, set_override model_ledger false, a new ModelLedger.from_dict(saved), then LEDGER.decorate gives speed '9.0 s' and health 'green' (expected '-' and 'idle'). The off ledger still saves 1912 bytes.

c2.title: A deferred proposal gets a new OVERRIDE record, street card and Gazette line on every council run, and 'deferred with 3 yes' is called an override while votes are still missing (round-1 finding not addressed)
c2.detail: The round-1 fix list does not mention this finding and does not reject it. CouncilLog.tally covers every proposal on the floor each run, and a deferred proposal stays on the floor. is_override('deferred', 3, 'live') is true whatever the number of votes cast. With the flag OFF (P4 is always on) a live Speaker that waits for the 2 mayors who have not voted yet shows 'Held Recycling Program despite 3 yes (override)' on the street card. The votes line says 'The Speaker went against the vote.' With mayor_context_v2 ON, the Gazette's feed also gets 'The Speaker went against the vote: Recycling Program OVERRIDE: deferred with 3 yes.' on every run. The 20-record history fills with identical rows and pushes real rulings out. Real cause: 3 yes of 3 votes cast, with 2 mayors still to vote, is not defiance, and the repeat is one stuck proposal counted again each run.
c2.repro: Measured. Harness r2/harn_e.gd (output r2/harn_e.log): PF.build with the flag on, brain.proposals = {recycling: votes argon, deepseek, kimi = yes}, and the Speaker scripted to reply {enact: []}. Run `await brain._run_council(day + k*3)` for k in 0..2. Result: 3 history records, each ['recycling','deferred',override=true,'OVERRIDE: deferred with 3 yes']; day_feed holds the 'went against the vote' line 3 times; council_words = 'Held Recycling Program despite 3 yes (override)'. Suggested fix: count a deferral as an override only with >=4 votes cast, or never; record a still-deferred proposal once, or replace its previous record.

c2.title: A stale vote note stays after the mayor flips the vote, and it is shown to every mayor and on the board with the new vote
c2.detail: _absorb_vote_notes only writes proposals[key]['notes'][me] when the reply carries a note for that key. If the mayor flips its vote in a later turn without a new note, the old reason survives. The REASONS GIVEN FOR VOTES line then pairs the new vote with the old reason, and the council record snapshot and the orbit board show the contradiction. Vote flips are the kind of event this feature exists to show, so the scenario is realistic. The effect is wrong data in other models' prompts and on screen, not a crash.
c2.repro: Measured (r2/harn_e.log, case B). Grok votes {curfew:'no'} with vote_notes {curfew:'kills nightlife'}. Next day Grok votes {curfew:'yes'} with no note. The proposal's notes stay {grok:'kills nightlife'} and mayor 0's prompt carries 'REASONS GIVEN FOR VOTES: curfew: Duke Granger (yes) "kills nightlife"'. Fix: when a vote is cast again, erase that mayor's note for the key before storing the new one.

c2.title: Orbit City Hall tab still re-renders its full text on every mayor decision, visible or not (round-1 finding not addressed)
c2.detail: The fix list neither fixes nor rejects this. city_hud.gd _on_mayor_decided still calls _render_council() unconditionally. That is five rebuilds of the council, board, record and notes text per dawn, plus the other triggers. The web build is frame-time sensitive. Only the call site was read; no cost was measured.
c2.repro: Read from the diff: `_render_council()  # the vote board shows each vote as it is cast` runs without a visibility or dirty check. A guard on tab visibility (render when the tab is shown) would keep the live-update behaviour.

The Gazette's model therefore reads 'The Speaker went against the vote: Recycling Program OVERRIDE: deferred with 3 yes.' That is redundant, shouty and awkward as input to a reporter prompt. Wording only.

c2.title: Replay (keyless demo) council card contradicts itself: headline 'Rejected Recycling Program', votes line lists all five mayors voting yes, and the quote says it passes
c2.detail: In a real replay ruling, the open street card read 'Rejected Recycling Program · Rejected Green Energy Subsidy · +2 more'. Under it the quote was the recorded statement 'Recycling passes with unanimous support...' and the votes line was 'Recycling Program: yes Ada, Viktor, Mei, Rosa, Duke'. The quiet-mode fix removed the word OVERRIDE and the count, but the card still shows 5 yes beside 'Rejected' and a statement that says 'passes'. The orbit record has the same look: 'Recycling Program: rejected (replay)' over a row of five green Y. This is the no-key and fallback path of the 12 Nov demo, and a viewer sees a council that rejects what everyone voted for, with no explanation. The REPLAY badge is small and does not explain it. A fix would be to drop the votes line for a quiet ruling, or to word it 'replayed ruling' on the card.

c2.title: A proposal that stays deferred adds a record and a Gazette line on every council run, so repeats fill the 20-record history and push real rulings out (round-1 finding, not closed)
c2.detail: CouncilLog.tally records every proposal still on the floor each run, and a deferred proposal is never erased. In the test city a scripted live Speaker that enacts nothing, with two stuck proposals (free_clinics 3 yes 0 no, trade_expo 1 yes 1 no), produced 12 records after 6 runs. All 12 were 'deferred', 6 of them marked OVERRIDE, and the Gazette feed got the identical line 'The Speaker went against the vote: Free Clinics OVERRIDE: deferred with 3 yes.' 6 times. After one real enactment (recycling), 20 more runs on one stuck proposal pushed the enactment out of council_history (it was gone, size 20). The docs say 'the last 20 rulings, one record per proposal'. The cap protects the save, but the City Hall 'Council record' (6 newest) fills with duplicate 'deferred' rows. A deferral with 3 yes and only 3 votes cast (two mayors yet to vote) is also called an OVERRIDE, which is false defiance in staggered street mode. The fix report listed this finding under neither fixed nor rejected. The unit's own test pins free_clinics 3 yes held back as 'OVERRIDE: deferred with 3 yes'.
c2.repro: Harness /tmp/claude-1000/-home-kunalsiyag-Ambassador-Gmi-Cloud-gridfall/4eb46f6b-fccd-4256-83c9-4c39144a74d2/scratchpad/c2/review-tests-claims/v2/h1.gd, output in h1.log (H1 lines: history 12, deferred 12, override 6, 6 identical feed lines, enactment displaced). Fix idea: write a deferred record only once per proposal or when its votes changed, and require 4 or more votes before a deferral can be an override.

c2.title: Seven tests of new behaviour survive their mutant (limits and guards that are documented but unpinned)
c2.detail: Each mutant left its test printing PASS, exit 0. (1) REQUEST_MAX 3000 changed to 30000: the '$3000 at most' cap in the flag text and the runbook is untested. (2) OPERATOR_DAYS 6 changed to 60: the Grid Operator line's staleness window is untested (the council and chaos windows are tested). (3) The league tie-break '-mi' changed to '+mi': ties are not tested. (4) The restore guard 'from == id' removed: a saved note from a mayor to itself loads. (5) The prune limit KEEP_DAYS 8 changed to 800: 'dropped after 8 days' in docs/save-schema.md is untested. (6) 'if held <= 0' changed to '< 0': a treasury of exactly $0 reads 'you hold $0 ... grant cannot be more than that' with a $N grant example, because only -300, 200 and 5000 are tested. (7) The 'amount > 0' guard on a request removed: a $0 request is stored. The amber WARN colour on OVERRIDE rows (council_board.gd) is also not pinned. get_parsed_text cannot see it, and nobody looked at pixels.
c2.repro: Apply one change to a scratch copy under the lock, then run godot --headless -s tools/tests/fp_mayor_context_test.gd. Examples: 'const REQUEST_MAX := 3000' to '30000', 'if held <= 0:' to 'if held < 0:', 'and day - int((n as Dictionary).get("day", -99)) <= KEEP_DAYS' to '<= 800'. Each gives exit 0. The mutation list and logs are in the v2 directory (M06, M12, M15, M17, M19, M20, M22, M31).

c3.title: Settle cap is not a cap: overlay held 11.3 s on a night-time Tab back (settle 9.2 s against the documented 'at most 6 s')
c3.detail: PlannerPrep._settle checks `last - began < SETTLE_CAP_MS` only after each frame completes, so a long frame in flight overshoots the cap by its whole length. In poke_new_1 the Planner was left at night (Day 4, 00:00) and Tab back took four freezes (2,050 ms at +2.1 s, 3,467 ms at +5.6 s, 1,900 ms at +7.5 s, 3,467 ms at +11.3 s). PLANNERPREP reported {"to_orbit":false,"settle":{"frames":9,"ms":9157.2,"calm":false},"ms":11224.8}: the card stood for 11.3 s (marks prepare_shown 154311, prepare_done 165536). The cap text appears in data/feature_flags.json ('at most 6 s'), planner_prep.gd (SETTLE_CAP_MS) and web-deploy.md. All four freezes were covered by the card, so the player was told, but 11 s of a dark card on a return to a night street is a long wait, and it suggests the street's night (lamp/spot) programs are not warmed (the warm-up states never reach 'unlit' in the 3 s budget). Normal daytime Tab backs held the card 4.5-5.4 s. One run; wave0 would show the same four bare freezes, so this is not a regression, only a false 'at most'. Fix: say 'at most 6 s plus the frame in flight', or hide the card when the elapsed time passes the cap even if the frame is pending is impossible, so document it; optionally warm the night state.
c3.lens: FREEZES AND BOOT IN TIME AND PIXELS, round 2 (headless Chrome, real GPU AMD Renoir iGPU, wave0 vs current web/smooth-freezes tree after the round-1 fixes; scratch /tmp/claude-1000/-home-kunalsiyag-Ambassador-Gmi-Cloud-gridfall/4eb46f6b-fccd-4256-83c9-4c39144a74d2/scratchpad/c3/review-freeze-measure/r2)

c3.title: One slow piece switches the drain off for about three game days
c3.detail: SpreadDrain keeps a running cost estimate that falls by 1% only on frames where run() is called and the frame is skipped. A single 25 ms piece raises the estimate (to 4.4 ms and above at 4x). After that, two sources of that cost no longer fit in the 8 ms budget, and the estimate only decays during dawn waits. A 25 ms hiccup (GC, a tab switch, a loaded machine) on the first brain piece of day 11 made days 12 and 13 keep the full 42 and 21 dawn frames, and day 14 about 25, at 4x. At 4x, pieces drained over 700 frames fell from 105 to 31 and days gained from +1.00 to +0.32 over the off run (5.75 vs 5.07 vs 4.75). At 8x, pieces fell from 135 to 33. Only pacing is affected, never state. The docs say 'probed again every 30 to 50 frames', which holds only for a 6 ms estimate; after a larger spike it takes many more skipped frames. Suggestion: reset the estimate at each day start, or let it decay per frame instead of per skipped dawn frame.

Output is in review-drain-correct/spike.log.

c3.title: 'No frame is longer than without the drain' does not hold: probe frames exceed it
c3.detail: When the estimate has decayed enough, a frame runs one or two extra pieces on top of the two forced ones to probe the cost. With 6 ms pieces (the browser-like case) this happened 1 to 2 times per 400 frames at 4x and 2 times at 8x. At 8x, p99 rose from 15.1 and 15.4 ms (off) to 17.2 and 17.6 ms (on) in both runs, and max was 18.8 and 18.2 vs 19.5 and 18.8. At 3 ms pieces and 4x, p99 went from 10.5 to 14.9 ms with 11 extra pieces. p95 is unchanged in every run (9.7 to 10.1 and 12.4 to 12.7), so the round-1 major is fixed. The remaining effect is a few frames per 400 over 16.7 ms. The wording in the flag description and web-deploy.md ('no frame is longer than without it', 'a frame already full of pieces gets none') should say 'at most a few probe frames'.

c3.title: fp_day_drain_test does not detect removal of the brain's busy_changed emit in CityBrain.drain_step
c3.detail: CityBrain._process used to emit busy_changed(pending_calls()) when the round's queue emptied; that logic moved into drain_step, which the drain scheduler now also calls. Deleting the two lines (`if _queue.is_empty(): busy_changed.emit(pending_calls())`) leaves FP_DAY_DRAIN_TEST: PASS and BRAIN_STALE_ANSWER_TEST: PASS. A regression would leave the HUD's mayors-busy indicator stuck after a day round. The hook tests assert order and wiring but not this side effect.
c3.repro: Back up city_brain.gd, delete lines 142-144 of the `drain_step` tail (the `if _queue.is_empty(): busy_changed.emit(...)` block), run tools/tests/fp_day_drain_test.gd and tools/tests/brain_stale_answer_test.gd: both PASS. Log: scratchpad/c3/review-tests-claims/mut.out (drainbusyemit).

c3.title: With warmup_orbit_variants off, an orbit state in the tuning still adds the Planner catalogue, and no test notices
c3.detail: shader_warmup.gd line 127 guards the catalogue with `WarmCollector.by_variant and _wants_orbit(states)`. Mutating it to `_wants_orbit(states)` passes fp_warmup_variants_test and fp_warmup_test. The flag-off test only checks the per-material recipe path and the large-scene skip, not that no catalogue is added when a tuning file asks for `orbit`. Only a probe-style tuning file can reach it, so no player is affected; it is a gap in the flag-off guarantee that the flag text states ("no Planner catalogue").
c3.repro: Replace the condition as above, run both warm-up tests: PASS. Log: mut.out (catalogue_flag).

c3.title: The PAINT_FRAMES assertion is tautological; the paint-before-heavy-frame guarantee is only checked against the constant itself
c3.detail: fp_planner_prep_test checks `frames_to_move >= PlannerPrep.PAINT_FRAMES`, so changing the constant cannot fail that line. Setting PAINT_FRAMES to 0 (overlay not painted before the heavy move, the behaviour the unit exists to prevent) failed the test run only by accident: other assertions failed and Godot exited 134 (a crash). A bare lowering to 1 would likely pass. A literal `>= 2` in the test would pin the claim 'painted for 2 frames'.
c3.repro: Set const PAINT_FRAMES := 0 and run the test: FAIL plus exit=134 (mut.out, paint0). Not run with 1.

c3.title: day_drain_fast ships default-on with no demonstrated benefit on the web, the platform the owner complained about
c3.detail: The native model gains 16-23% at 4x and 0-13% at 8x, with the clock parked at dawn for 9-10 frames instead of 42. In the browser, pieces cost 5-10 ms, the scheduler counts forced pieces against an 8 ms budget and so adds almost nothing (6 ms stand-in: 1-2 extra pieces in 400 frames). The docs say this honestly ("no browser pace gain is claimed"; the browser table is of the first, replaced version). The brief's item 3 for the day-start stall therefore remains unmet on the web. It is default-on code in the sim hot path (CitySim._process_sliced, two new step hooks) with its measured cost near zero. The risk is review burden, not a defect.
c3.repro: Read docs/runbooks/web-deploy.md 'Fast-forward drain'. The shipped scheduler was never re-run in the browser (the implementer says the lock queue was over an hour).
